strengths: Novel and well-motivated approach: Uses learned intrinsic token importance for KV cache eviction rather than myopic recent-attention-based methods, with clear practical motivation for long-context inference

Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation: Extensive experiments across math reasoning, long procedural generation, and long-context understanding benchmarks with consistent improvements (matching full cache at ~25% KV budget)

Exceptional qualitative analysis: Detailed visualizations (Figures 12-26) revealing interpretable learned patterns that align with human intuition and demonstrate emergent heuristics like attention sinks and sliding windows
Technically sound design: Elegant exponential decay formulation inspired by cognitive science, principled joint training with distillation and capacity loss, minimal added parameters
Strong empirical results: TRIM-KV consistently outperforms multiple baselines across diverse settings, and even surpasses full-cache models in some cases, with hardware-efficient implementation
Practical impact and reproducibility: Addresses real memory bottleneck for long-context inference, commits to code release, provides detailed experimental protocols and hyperparameter specifications
Thorough ablation studies: Comprehensive analysis of loss components, architecture choices, and key hyperparameters with clear visualization of design decisions
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: Retention gate is essentially an MLP outputting scalar scores; exponential decay borrowed from cognitive science; similar importance-based ideas explored in attention sparsity literature
Insufficient training cost analysis: No clear reporting of training time overhead or computational cost of joint gate optimization; freezing backbone parameters limits model adaptation

Generalization concerns: Gates trained on OpenR1-MATH-220K; heavy evaluation focus on Qwen family models; unclear transfer to other model architectures (Llama, Claude) and domains; no cross-model evaluation

Missing statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; some non-monotonic behaviors unexplained; single-run evaluations for certain experiments; high variance results lack characterization
Incomplete failure mode analysis: Limited explanation of when/why TRIM-KV underperforms full cache (especially on long-context tasks); non-monotonic performance in some settings left unexplained

Hyperparameter complexity with insufficient sensitivity analysis: Multiple hyperparameters (M, λ_cap, β, gate architecture) introduced but limited analysis of sensitivity; practical guidance for setting M on new tasks sparse

Evaluation limitations: Long-context benchmarks are modest (LongMemEval: 125K tokens; SCBench query-dependent); missing recent learnable baselines; KeyDiff baseline limited to query-agnostic comparison

Theoretical justification gaps: Why creation-time importance determines lifelong token value lacks formal analysis; connection between forgetting curves and transformer attention patterns not rigorously established

strengths: Addresses a practically important problem: memory-bounded KV cache management for long-context LLM inference
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse benchmarks (math reasoning, long generation, long-context understanding) with strong empirical results, especially in low-memory regimes
Valuable qualitative analysis revealing learned layer and head-specific specializations in token retention patterns
Practical implementation: hardware-aware, compatible with existing kernels (FlashAttention), minimal computational overhead (~2% throughput)
Well-structured paper with reproducibility considerations, implementation details in appendices, and plans to release code
Reasonable technical design combining exponential decay with lightweight neural networks for importance scoring
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: Learning what to keep in cache is a straightforward idea; retention gates are simple MLPs; exponential decay is direct application of existing memory models

Critical training-inference mismatch: Retention gates trained exclusively on math reasoning (OpenR1-Math) but evaluated on completely different tasks (long generation, conversation understanding); generalization to other domains not thoroughly validated

Experimental fairness concerns: Baseline comparisons lack clarity on training procedures; different baselines use different training paradigms; inconsistent evaluation settings; unclear whether all baselines had similar training budgets

Heavy emphasis on math reasoning benchmarks (AIME24, GSM8K, MATH-500) which are primarily symbolic reasoning tasks, not true long-context understanding; long-context importance is minimal in these tasks, biasing evaluation

Incomplete technical justification: Capacity loss formulation (Eq. 5) connection to strict budgets is loose; hyperparameter choices (λ_cap=1.0, M=512) appear arbitrary; β learning procedure not clearly explained; retention computed at creation time may miss important context
Limited ablation studies: No systematic investigation of training dataset sensitivity; minimal architectural exploration; no ablation on creation-time vs. inference-time importance scoring

Generalization limitations: Assumption that 'intrinsic importance at creation time' generalizes across domains not rigorously validated; Figure 8 shows degradation when trained on non-math data but investigation is limited

Evaluation scope limitations: Long-context testing up to 128K still relatively short; chunked-prefill analysis (Section B.3) is practical but minimal; no analysis on extremely long sequences or failure modes

Excellent interpretability analysis with rich qualitative visualizations showing learned retention scores align with human intuition (problem descriptions high, stopwords low) and emergent patterns like sliding windows appear organically
Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning three task categories (math reasoning, long-context, long-generation) with thorough ablation studies

strengths: Addresses a genuine and important problem in long-context LLM inference (KV cache memory bottleneck)

Well-designed qualitative analysis with interpretable visualizations of learned retention patterns (Figures 11-19) showing alignment with human intuition
